name.description: Uniquely identifies a layer 1 settings profile

IngressPfc.description:
Ingress-side PFC configuration for a port.
EITHER (a) `priorities` to enable + configure PFC TX, OR (b) `clear: true`
to explicitly disable PFC TX on this port. Mutually exclusive with `ingress_pause`.
When clear is true, the TM service tears down any PPGs allocated for this port
and resets MAC TX bitmap; the fwding service deletes any PFC_CLASSIFY_TBL
entries previously installed for this port's traffic.

clear.description:
When true, disables PFC TX on this port and clears classifier entries.
Mutually exclusive with `priorities`.

IngressPfcPriority.description:
Per-priority ingress PFC settings. A priority entry uses Tier 1 (priority only),
Tier 2 (friendly threshold knobs), or Tier 3 (raw cells).
Tier 2 (friendly) and Tier 3 (raw cells) are mutually exclusive — enforced
by the api-server resolver layer (tm_profiles.py), NOT by this schema.
This schema permits both sets of fields; the resolver rejects mixed
input with HTTP 400.

Classifier match (independent of tier): `tos` + `mask` define the ternary
match against the outer-IPv4 diffserv byte (`ig_md.encap_diffserv`) used by
`pfc_classify_tbl` to decide which traffic gets routed to this priority's
PPG and egress queue. Default `tos=0, mask=255` matches exactly diffserv=0;
callers normally override to match their target DSCP pattern (e.g.,
`tos=16, mask=252` matches DSCP=4 ignoring ECN bits).

priority.description:
iCoS priority class (0-7). Drives `INGRESS_COS` + `EGRESS_QID` action
params in PFC_CLASSIFY_TBL (api-server enforces them equal at translation),
which in turn drives PPG selection (TM TX side) and egress queue +
`pfc_cos` honor (TM RX side).

tos.description:
Raw 8-bit outer-IPv4 ToS / DiffServ value to match. Caller's
responsibility to choose this in conjunction with `mask`.

mask.description:
Ternary mask for `tos`. 0xFF (255) = exact byte match, 0xFC (252) =
match DSCP ignoring ECN bits, 0xE0 (224) = match top 3 bits (class
selector range). No validation of `tos & mask == tos`.

upper_threshold_pct.description:
PFC fires when PPG buffer is this % of total capacity.
Default 50 (Sai-equivalent). OpenAPI 3.0 boolean form for
strict-greater-than-zero, strict-less-than-100.

lower_threshold_pct.description:
PFC clears when PPG buffer drains to this % of total capacity.
Must be less than upper_threshold_pct (enforced by resolver).
Default 40 (Sai-equivalent).

guaranteed_cells.description:
Cells guaranteed to this PPG. Raw-tier override; takes precedence over
friendly knobs (which would be rejected if both present on same entry).

EgressPfc.description:
Egress-side PFC configuration for a port.
EITHER (a) `priorities` to enable + configure PFC RX (honor incoming PFC
frames), OR (b) `clear: true` to explicitly disable PFC RX on this port
(triggers ClearPfcConfig in TM service: reset queue pfc_cos mappings,
clear MAC RX bitmap, clear latched scheduler state). Mutually exclusive
with `egress_pause`.

clear.description: When true, disables PFC RX on this port. Mutually exclusive with `priorities`.

EgressPfcPriority.description:
Per-priority egress PFC settings. Tier 1 (priority only) / Tier 2 (queue_buffer_us)
/ Tier 3 (raw cells).
Tier 2 (friendly) and Tier 3 (raw cells) are mutually exclusive — enforced
by the api-server resolver layer (tm_profiles.py), NOT by this schema.
This schema permits both sets of fields; the resolver rejects mixed
input with HTTP 400.

queue_buffer_us.description:
Microseconds of guaranteed TX buffer at port line rate. Default 1.0
(= Sai's 72 cells @ 100G). OpenAPI 3.0 boolean form for
strict-greater-than-zero.

IngressPause.description:
Ingress-side 802.3x Global Pause configuration for a port.
EITHER (a) `enable: true` to turn on Global Pause generation, OR
(b) `clear: true` to explicitly disable it. Mutually exclusive with
`ingress_pfc` on the same port — the TM service's flow-control mode
for a port is either 802.1Qbb PFC or 802.3x Global Pause, never both
at once (see soda-bfs-tm-service pfc_controller.cc
ConfigurePortFlowControl()).

KNOWN BACKEND LIMITATION (UHDCONNECT-423): the underlying
`PortPfcConfig.enable_global_pause` proto field is a single flag —
setting it true arms BOTH the TX (generate) and RX (honor) MAC-level
pause behavior together (`bf_pal_port_flow_control_link_pause_set`
is called with both `pause_tx=true` and `pause_rx=true`
unconditionally). There is currently no way to enable one direction
without the other. Setting `ingress_pause.enable: true` alone (with
no `egress_pause` block) will still cause this port to honor received
802.3x PAUSE frames as a side effect of the shared backend flag.

enable.description:
When true, enables 802.3x Global Pause generation (TX) on this
port. Mutually exclusive with `clear`.

clear.description:
When true, disables Global Pause on this port (subject to the
same shared-flag limitation described above — if the paired
direction, e.g. `egress_pause`, is still enabled on this port,
Global Pause remains active overall). Mutually exclusive with
`enable`.

EgressPause.description:
Egress-side 802.3x Global Pause configuration for a port.
EITHER (a) `enable: true` to turn on Global Pause honor (RX) — UHD
stops transmitting on this port while a received PAUSE frame's timer
is active — OR (b) `clear: true` to explicitly disable it. Mutually
exclusive with `egress_pfc` on the same port — the TM service's
flow-control mode for a port is either 802.1Qbb PFC or 802.3x Global
Pause, never both at once (see soda-bfs-tm-service pfc_controller.cc
ConfigurePortFlowControl()).

KNOWN BACKEND LIMITATION (UHDCONNECT-423): the underlying
`PortPfcConfig.enable_global_pause` proto field is a single flag —
setting it true arms BOTH the RX (honor) and TX (generate) MAC-level
pause behavior together (`bf_pal_port_flow_control_link_pause_set`
is called with both `pause_rx=true` and `pause_tx=true`
unconditionally). There is currently no way to enable one direction
without the other. Setting `egress_pause.enable: true` alone (with
no `ingress_pause` block) will still cause this port to generate
802.3x PAUSE frames upstream as a side effect of the shared backend
flag.

enable.description:
When true, enables 802.3x Global Pause honor (RX) on this port —
this is the fix for UHDCONNECT-423. Mutually exclusive with
`clear`.

clear.description:
When true, disables Global Pause honor on this port (subject to
the same shared-flag limitation described above — if the paired
direction, e.g. `ingress_pause`, is still enabled on this port,
Global Pause remains active overall). Mutually exclusive with
`enable`.

For breakout mode, this value must be specified,  and the range of channels must not overlap with any other range of channels on  the same front-panel port. If num_channels is omitted or set to 0 the UHD will  use a default based on the port speed

FrontPanelPortGroup.description:
A list of front-panel ports to represent multiple ports with a single port_name. This allows connection types to accept a set of ports instead of a single port, but not all connection types accept groups.
The ingress distribution setting specifies how the configuration is to be distributed to the ports. The configuration (e.g. the vlans to route) can be either copied or split equally amongst the ingress ports. Split is the default, as would typically be the case for non-lag port groups, where traffic is unique on each port. Copy is typically used for lag port groups, where traffic might be sent to any port.
Egress distribution is always split. All egress ports must have link up to avoid a loss of traffic (assuming ingress traffic is uniformly distributed).

ConnectVlanVxlan.description:
Reencapsulates VLan traffic to VxLAN traffic between two endpoints. This can be useful when connecting equipment that supports VLAN but not VxLAN to equipment that requires VxLAN.
One of the endpoints must be tagged "vlan", and the other "vxlan". Traffic arriving on the vlan-tagged endpoint is reencapsulated and sent to the vxlan-tagged endpoint using the VLAN ID of the traffic to determine the VNI of the untagged endpoint. Likewise, traffic from the vxlan-tagged endpoint is reencapsulated as VLAN traffic with the VLAN ID for the vlan-tagged endpoint being derived from the VNI of the VxLAN traffic from the vxlan-tagged endpoint.
If the traffic received on a vxlan-tagged endpoint arrives on a VLAN (of the outermost Ethernet), the VLAN will be discarded. And the traffic will appear on the VLAN of the vlan-tagged endpoint. If the inner, VxLAN-enclosed, packet is on a VLAN, then that. will become the inner VLAN of the traffic exiting the vlan-tagged endpoint.
If the traffic arriving on the vlan-tagged endpoint is Q-in-Q, then the inner VLAN ID becomes the outer VLAN of the VxLAN-encapsulated packet leaving the vxlan-tagged port.
The vxlan_settings that are configured as ranges need only specify the start value, in which case the count will be the vlan count of the vlan-tagged endpoint.

VxlanSettings.description: The properties of a VxLAN endpoint which will be reencapsulated as VLAN traffic on the other (VLAN) endpoint. This requires specifying the VNI or range of VNIs to match with and to be used to populate the VLAN or range of VLANs on the other endpoint.

vni.description: The VNI of the VxLAN header, or an open-ended range thereof that applies to the associated endpoint.

protocol_id.description: (Optional) IP protocol ID to filter on (e.g., 6=TCP, 17=UDP, 1=ICMP). If specified along with 'protocols', this field takes precedence. Use with src_port and/or dst_port for L4 filtering.

src_port.description: (Optional) L4 source port to filter on. Only applies when protocol_id is TCP(6) or UDP(17). If specified, only packets with matching source port are processed.

dst_port.description: (Optional) L4 destination port to filter on. Only applies when protocol_id is TCP(6) or UDP(17). If specified, only packets with matching destination port are processed.

ProtocolFilter.description: Filters to accept or reject traffic based on the inner VxLAN packet. If both lists are empty specified, then all protocols are accepted. Otherwise only one list may be specified.

accept.description: A list of protocols to accept or reject from the inner VxLAN packet. The protocols are not from any specific layer of the stack. For example BGP runs on TCP, so if tcp is specified, then there is no point in specifying bgp.

reject.description: A list of protocols to accept or reject from the inner VxLAN packet. The protocols are not from any specific layer of the stack. For example BGP runs on TCP, so if tcp is specified, then there is no point in specifying bgp.

Minimal shared base for per-function VLAN settings. Encap functions (connect_vlan_vxlan / connect_vlan_nvgre) extend this with their own routing/protocol-filter fields (see VxlanVlanSettings / NvgreVlanSettings).

protocol_id.description: (Optional) IP protocol ID to filter on (e.g., 6=TCP, 17=UDP, 1=ICMP). Only packets matching this protocol are encapsulated. Use with src_port and/or dst_port for L4 filtering.

dst_port.description: (Optional) L4 destination port to filter on. Only applies when protocol_id is TCP(6) or UDP(17). If specified, only packets with matching destination port are encapsulated.

OutgoingVxlanHeader.description:
The Ethernet and IP headers to populate the outer VxLAN envelope. These ranges are mapped from the VLAN range for the endpoint in the same way as tunnel IDs.
Use src_ip and dst_ip with choice "ipv4" or "ipv4_range" for an IPv4 underlay, or "ipv6" or "ipv6_range" for an IPv6 underlay. Both src_ip and dst_ip must use the same address family.

src_mac.description: The source MAC address for the injected Ethernet header, or an open-ended range thereof that maps to the src_vlan range.

src_ip.description: The source IP address for the injected IP header, or an open-ended range thereof that maps to the src_vlan range. Use choice "ipv4"/"ipv4_range" for IPv4 underlay or "ipv6"/"ipv6_range" for IPv6 underlay.

dst_mac.description: The next-hop MAC address for the injected Ethernet header, or an open-ended range thereof that maps to the src_vlan range.

dst_ip.description: The IP address for the injected IP header or an open-ended range thereof that maps to the src_vlan range. Use choice "ipv4"/"ipv4_range" for IPv4 underlay or "ipv6"/"ipv6_range" for IPv6 underlay.

tos.description: (Optional) The TOS/DSCP value to set in the IP header of the outer VxLAN envelope. If not specified, the value will be set to 0. For an IPv6 underlay this sets the IPv6 Traffic Class byte.

udp_src_port.description: The source UDP port for the VxLAN header. The default value is 0, If field is not provided by user than source port is calculated as a hash of the following fields: - For IPv4: inner source IP address, inner destination IP address, and protocol. - For IPv6: inner source IP address, inner destination IP address, and next header.

udp_dst_port.description: The destination UDP port for the VxLAN header. The default value is 4789.

ConnectVlanNvgre.description:
Reencapsulates VLan traffic to NVGRE traffic between two endpoints. This can be useful when connecting equipment that supports VLAN but not NVGRE to equipment that requires NVGRE.
One of the endpoints must be tagged "vlan", and the other "nvgre". Traffic arriving on the vlan-tagged endpoint is reencapsulated and sent to the NVGRE-tagged endpoint using the VLAN ID of the traffic to determine the VSID of the untagged endpoint. Likewise, traffic from the nvgre-tagged endpoint is reencapsulated as VLAN traffic with the VLAN ID for the vlan-tagged endpoint being derived from the VSID of the NVGRE traffic from the NVGRE-tagged endpoint.
If the traffic received on a NVGRE-tagged endpoint arrives on a VLAN (of the outermost Ethernet), the VLAN will be discarded. And the traffic will appear on the VLAN of the vlan-tagged endpoint. If the inner, NVGRE-enclosed, packet is on a VLAN, then that will become the inner VLAN of the traffic exiting the vlan-tagged endpoint.
If the traffic arriving on the vlan-tagged endpoint is Q-in-Q, then the inner VLAN ID becomes the outer VLAN of the NVGRE-encapsulated packet leaving the nvgre-tagged port.
The nvgre_settings that are configured as ranges need only specify the start value, in which case the count will be the vlan count of the vlan-tagged endpoint.

The Ethernet and IP headers to populate the outer NVGRE envelope. These ranges are mapped from the VLAN range for the endpoint in the same way as tunnel IDs.
Use src_ip and dst_ip with choice "ipv4" or "ipv4_range" for an IPv4 underlay, or "ipv6" or "ipv6_range" for an IPv6 underlay. Both src_ip and dst_ip must use the same address family.

Connection.description:
A two-or-more-way connection between Ethernet ports that optionally transforms the data (i.e. a "bump in the wire").
Multiple connections can connect to any given port, but the transforms for source ports should be uniquely specified to avoid undefined behavior. For example, a single source port might use two ARP  connections going to two different destination ports. In that case one connection could route VLAN ARPs and the other could route non_VLAN ARPs (or a different range of ARPs) so that each  would carries unique traffic.
All connection types can perform encap/decap of VLAN traffic bidirectionally. Some connection types can perform encap/decap to/from other protocols as well. The term tunnel ID in the following descriptions is used to describe either VLAN IDs or the tunnel identifiers of other protocols (e.g. VNIs for VxLAN).
Traffic arriving on an endpoint with a tunnel IDs outside of the ID or range specified in an endpoint's configuration are ignored. Additional connections may be added with non-overlapping sets of tunnel IDs to route and/or process different sets differently.
When an endpoint is specified with a single tunnel ID, and a packet arrives at that endpoint with a matching ID, then the packet is routed to the opposite endpoint(s) and receives the tunnel ID (or first ID of a range) of the opposite endpoint.
When an endpoint is specified with a range of tunnel IDs, and a packet arrives that endpoint with a matching ID, then the offset from the start of that endpoint's range. The packet is  routed to the opposite endpoint(s) and receives the tunnel ID from the opposite endpoint's  tunnel ID or range. If the opposite endpoint is a single ID, then, of course, that is the outgoing tunnel ID. If it is a range, however, then the offset from the incoming endpoint is added to the start of the outgoing endpoint's range. If only one of the endpoints has a count, then that count is used for both. If two endpoints have a different count, however, then the outgoing tunnel ID is according to the following equation:
tunnel_id_out = tunnel_id_in + ( input_offset modulo range_count_out )
So if the incoming range is less than the outgoing range count, then the result is the same as if the counts were the same. But if the it is the outgoing range count is smaller, then the incoming ranges are wrapped around.

name.description: Unique name of an object. It also serves as the primary key for arrays of objects.

Endpoint.description: Elements of ingress and/or egress for a connection. Consists of a single front-panel port and a set of tags that some connections might require to identify specific endpoints. VLAN placement (single or double) is configured per-function via that function's own settings block (e.g. `vlan_endpoint_settings` for encap, `vlan_endpoint_settings_port1`/ `vlan_endpoint_settings_port2` for passthrough), not on the endpoint itself.

port_name.description:
The name of the port used by this endpoint.

x-constraint:
- /components/schemas/Port/properties/name

tags.description: A list of tags (strings) to distinguish this endpoint from others. For example used by vxlan_settings to identify applicable endpoints.

Function.description: One of a list of functions to be applied to a connection's endpoints

ConnectEthernet.description: Connect Ethernet packets between two endpoints.

ethertypes.description: A list of Ethernet types. An empty list means allow all ethertypes.

vlan_endpoint_settings_port1.description: The VLAN (single or, via two functions[] entries, Q-in-Q) to match/apply on port1 (connection.endpoints[0]) of the passthrough. Optional; absence or `non_vlan` means untagged traffic on this port.

vlan_endpoint_settings_port2.description: The VLAN (single or, via two functions[] entries, Q-in-Q) to match/apply on port2 (connection.endpoints[1]) of the passthrough. Optional; absence or `non_vlan` means untagged traffic on this port.

dst_mac_endpoint_settings_port1.description: Optional destination MAC address(es) reachable on port1 (connection.endpoints[0]). Mutually exclusive with vlan_endpoint_settings_port1/port2 anywhere in this connection (see validation below). Absent means dst_mac routing is not active on this port, and this connection's traffic passes through unrestricted (subject only to ethertypes, if set). When present, this is RESTRICTIVE, not additive: only traffic whose destination MAC matches one of the configured address(es) is forwarded on this port -- all other traffic (including any not matching another dst_mac_endpoint_settings_* entry) is dropped. The generic ingress-port passthrough entries are not installed for this connection in that case.

dst_mac_endpoint_settings_port2.description: Optional destination MAC address(es) reachable on port2 (connection.endpoints[1]). See dst_mac_endpoint_settings_port1.

PortDstMacSettings.description: Per-port destination-MAC-routing settings for connect_ethernet (dst_mac_endpoint_settings_port1/_port2). NOT to be confused with the unrelated, pre-existing "mac_routing" routing_method selector under connect_vlan_vxlan/connect_vlan_nvgre (VxlanMacRoutingSettings / VlanMacRoutingSettings) -- that is a VLAN/VNI-selection mechanism keyed off src/dst MAC. This PortDstMacSettings is a completely separate concept: a per-port ternary DESTINATION-MAC match added directly to connect_ethernet's passthrough table (see UHDCONNECT-429). Named `dst_mac` explicitly (rather than just `mac`) because this feature always matches destination MAC -- never source MAC -- and the field name should make that unambiguous to API consumers.

Config.description: A container for all models that are part of the configuration.

connections.description: A two-or-more-way protocol-specific connection between Ethernet endpoints  that optionally transforms the data along the way. Multiple connections can attach to a single port/endpoint, but the connections should be mutually exclusive. For example, a single source endpoint might use two ARP  connections going to two different destination endpoint. In that case one connection could route VLAN ARPs and the other could route non_VLAN ARPS (or a different range of VLAN IDs) so that each  connection carries unique traffic.

Profiles.description: Profiles are reusable settings that can be referenced by name

layer_1_profiles.description: A list of available layer1 settings that can be applied to ports.
